Class LPCObjectLifecycle

java.lang.Object
io.github.protasm.jvmud.engine.instance.lpc.LPCObjectLifecycle
public final class LPCObjectLifecycle extends Object
Keeps a live LPC object's identity stable while its executable receiver changes.

The first materialized receiver remains the identity used by LPC references and by engine world, session, command and timer bindings. A reload prepares another receiver, copies compatible field state, then installs its revision without destroying that identity. Creation hooks and LPC field initializers are deliberately absent from this operation: replacing behavior must not recreate residents, reset game state or repeat external effects.

Historical receiver aliases use weak identity keys. An old closure keeps its captured receiver available, but the alias registry alone does not retain every replaced receiver or revision. The original identity and the currently installed receiver remain strongly owned while the object is live; in particular, its original generated class is not reclaimable while that identity exists.

This owner is confined to the mudlib's execution lane. It does not provide independent thread safety or general rollback of arbitrary LPC execution.

    • prepareReload

      public LPCObjectLifecycle.PreparedReload prepareReload(Object object, LPCProgramRevision revision)
      Creates a replacement receiver and transfers state without changing the live object.

      Every non-static, non-synthetic field must retain its declaring program, name and JVM type. Rejecting schema changes makes migration deliberate rather than silently dropping or reinterpreting live state. Generated constructors perform only Java allocation; LPC creation hooks and field initialization are not run.

    • install

      public void install(LPCObjectLifecycle.PreparedReload prepared)
      Installs a prepared revision after verifying its receiver and refreshing the latest live state. State validation and transfer finish before the live behavior mapping changes.

    • withReceiver

      public <T> T withReceiver(Object receiver, Supplier<T> action)
      Runs code captured by a historical receiver against the live object's current field state.

      Inline closures retain their original generated helper and class. During such a call, state is copied into that receiver and nested calls on the same identity use its revision. The resulting state is copied back even when the closure throws. Named-method callables instead follow ordinary dispatch to the currently installed revision.

    • remove

      public void remove(Object object)
      Removes executable state when an object is destroyed, retaining its historical identity.

      Stored closures and references can outlive destruction. Their receivers must still resolve to the destroyed identity so the host's tombstone checks cannot mistake them for live objects. The host already retains destroyed identities for that same reason.
